key_insight: Collaborating AI agents autonomously derived and experimentally tested a calibration result for diamond quantum-spin ensembles while rejecting evidence compromised by signal drift.
engineering_relevance: Peer-checking agents could improve automated quantum-hardware characterization by combining theoretical validation, discriminating experiments and drift-aware measurement protocols.
method: Generate and critique research questions, with authority to stop or redirect investigations.
Derive the minimum calibration settings for a defined microwave-pulse family and check the result computationally.
Test competing predictions experimentally and revise measurements when reference signals reveal drift.
evidence_signal: The initial experiment was deemed inconclusive because repeated reference measurements revealed drift; a revised experiment met unchanged acceptance criteria and supported the theoretical predictions.
watch_item: The demonstration concerns a defined pulse-sequence family in diamond spin ensembles; broader reliability across quantum platforms remains unestablished.
paper_title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
